_comment: Declarative validator rule pack. Each rule is an instance of a generic template executor in app/validation/rule_engine.py. Rules contain NO medical codes — only descriptor grammar, language lexicons, structural patterns, and authority citations. New rules of an existing template are added here (config change), not in Python.

rules.authority: CMS Claims Processing Manual Ch.13 (review of prior films is E/M data work); CMS global surgery package (intraoperative/confirmation imaging is included in the procedure)
rules._raw_text_why: negation of FINDINGS ('no fracture identified on AP/lateral views') does not negate the study having been performed, so the negation scrub must not eat the evidence

action.message: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} removed — every mention of this modality in the note is a non-billable context ({contexts}): prior-visit films are E/M data review, ordered/future studies weren't rendered today, and intraoperative/post-procedure confirmation imaging is included in the surgical package.
action.recommendation: Bill imaging only for a diagnostic study performed and interpreted at this encounter with documented findings

rules.authority: CPT surgery guidelines: wound debridement is reported by the deepest tissue level removed; an audit pays only the level the documentation supports

family._strip_why: the '(includes epidermis and dermis...)' parenthetical names the SHALLOWER layers a code subsumes, not its own level

rules._tiers_why: fixed human anatomy ordering — a language/anatomy lexicon, and the exact tissue words the AMA descriptors themselves use

evidence._ignore_why: a tissue word owned by a different same-sentence procedure ('bone biopsy', 'bone cultures') is not evidence of debridement depth

action.message: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} ('{desc}') bills a tissue level the note does not document — {evidence}; {action}. CPT reports debridement by the deepest tissue level removed AND documented.
action.evidence_found: the deepest tissue documented in a debridement sentence is '{word}'
action.evidence_missing: no tissue level is documented in any debridement sentence
action.action_dup: line removed — {target} (already on the claim) is the supportable member
action.recommendation: Document the deepest tissue level actually debrided (subcutaneous/fascia/muscle/bone) and re-bill that level

rules.authority: ICD-10-CM guideline I.A.15 ('with' convention: Index subterms under 'with' are presumed linked) and I.C.4.a (assign as many codes from the category as needed for all associated conditions)

index_link._extra_token_why: site/qualifier words beyond the axis itself must match the billed companion's own descriptor ('foot' → foot-ulcer L-codes); only pure grammar words are dropped, NOT the site vocabulary

add.rationale: AUTO-ADDED: the claim carries a {family} diabetes code and a skin-ulcer code; ICD-10-CM's 'with' convention (guideline I.A.15) presumes the link, and I.C.4.a requires the combination code.
add.review_reason: Confirm {code} — added per the with-convention; only a provider statement that the ulcer is unrelated to the diabetes overrides it

action.message: AUTO-ADDED: {code} ('{desc}') — the claim carries both a diabetes code and a skin-ulcer code, and the Alphabetic Index links them under 'with' (presumed related per guideline I.A.15); the combination code is required unless the provider states the conditions are unrelated.
action.recommendation: Confirm and keep {code} per the with-convention

rules.authority: NCCI Policy Manual Ch.1: services integral to a surgical procedure — including debridement of the operative site and wound margins — are included in the procedure's payment and not separately reportable
rules._raw_text_why: margin-preparation wording ('wound margins debrided to bleeding tissue') contains no negation to scrub, and the gate must see the sentence exactly as written

action.message: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} removed — every debridement mention in the note is operative-field margin/edge preparation ({contexts}) of a same-claim surgical procedure; NCCI Policy Manual Ch.1 includes debridement of the operative site in the surgery's payment.
action.recommendation: Bill debridement separately only for a distinct wound outside the operative field, documented with its own site, instruments, and endpoint

rules.authority: ICD-10-CM L97/L98.4 severity axis: the final character encodes the deepest tissue layer involved, per the descriptors' own tier words; code only the depth the documentation supports (guideline I.B, code to the highest level of specificity DOCUMENTED)
rules._tiers_why: the exact tissue words the ICD-10-CM descriptors themselves use ('limited to breakdown of skin' / 'fat layer exposed' / 'necrosis of muscle' / 'necrosis of bone') — fixed human anatomy ordering, not a curated code list

action.message: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} swapped to {target} ('{desc}') — {evidence}. The ICD-10-CM ulcer codes' final character encodes the deepest tissue layer, and an audit pays only the depth the documentation supports.
action.evidence_found: the deepest tissue documented in an ulcer sentence is '{word}'
action.evidence_missing: no ulcer sentence documents any deeper tissue layer, so only the shallowest tier is supportable
action.recommendation: Document the deepest tissue layer involved (skin breakdown/fat/muscle/bone) and bill {target} only if that depth is stated

rules.authority: ICD-10-CM guideline IV.J (code conditions the encounter addresses) enforced at the classification's own residual markers; CMS-1500 adjudication — an unpointed, unmandated secondary cannot change payment
rules._residual_why: the classification's own markers for codes without a specific documented entity; specific-entity siblings are the sibling checks' turf

action.message: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} ('{desc}') moved from the billed diagnoses to supporting_conditions — a residual-category ('unspecified'/'other specified') secondary that the assessment/imaging never documents and no billed code's Tabular instruction mandates. It remains recorded for the coder.
action.review_reason: Demoted from billed diagnoses: residual-category code not documented in the assessment/imaging and not mandated by any billed code's Tabular instructions
action.recommendation: If the provider addressed this condition today, document it in the assessment and re-bill

rules.authority: CPT descriptor for Achilles tendon repair codes explicitly limits the code to repair of a RUPTURED Achilles tendon; CPT/CMS correct-coding principles require the billed procedure match the pathology actually documented in the operative note, not merely a related tendon procedure

action.message_added: AUTO-ADDED: {code} ('{desc}') added — the note documents an acute Achilles tendon rupture repaired at this encounter.
action.message_undocumented: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} ('{desc}') removed — this descriptor requires repair of a RUPTURED Achilles tendon, but no note sentence documents an acute tendon rupture; the operative findings and procedure describe chronic Haglund's deformity with insertional Achilles tendinopathy (detachment, debridement of degenerative tissue, and reattachment for exostectomy exposure), which is not reported under a rupture-repair code.
action.rationale_added: Note sentence(s) affirmatively document an Achilles tendon rupture repaired today.
action.review_reason_added: Confirm {code} — verify the operative note documents an acute rupture, not chronic tendinopathy/detachment for exostectomy exposure.
action.recommendation: Code the procedure actually performed (calcaneal exostectomy with tendon debridement/reattachment) rather than a rupture-repair code unless an acute Achilles rupture is documented

provenance.rationale: CPT 27650 is defined by its own descriptor as repair of a RUPTURED Achilles tendon. The note never documents a tendon rupture anywhere — the pathology described throughout is Haglund's deformity with retrocalcaneal bursitis and chronic insertional Achilles tendinopathy, and the operative note describes detaching/elevating the tendon to expose the calcaneus for exostectomy, debriding degenerative tissue, then reattaching with suture anchors. That is a chronic degenerative repair/reattachment, not repair of an acute rupture, so the descriptor's own defining term is undocumented. This is exactly the documented_service_completion mechanism: select the family by descriptor grammar requiring the defining clinical term, look for note evidence naming that exact pathology (negation-scrubbed), and suppress the billed line when no sentence documents it. The rule never hard-codes 27650 — it targets any 27xxx-range procedure code whose descriptor requires a documented 'ruptured Achilles' finding.

rules.authority: CPT descriptor for limited bilateral noninvasive physiologic extremity arterial studies mandates ABI at distal posterior tibial/anterior tibial-dorsalis pedis arteries plus Doppler waveform recording/analysis (or plethysmography, or transcutaneous oxygen tension) at 1-2 levels; CMS correct-coding principles require the billed procedure match a study affirmatively documented as performed at the encounter, not merely a diagnosis of vascular disease

exclusions.label: history/PMH statement only
exclusions.regex: \b(history of|past medical history|h/o)\b.{0,30}(peripheral arterial disease|pad|vascular disease)\b

action.message_added: AUTO-ADDED: {code} ('{desc}') added — the note documents an ankle-brachial index and Doppler waveform study performed at this encounter, matching this descriptor's own required elements.
action.message_undocumented: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} ('{desc}') removed — no note sentence documents the ABI plus Doppler waveform/plethysmography/transcutaneous oxygen study this descriptor requires; a bare 'peripheral arterial disease' history or diminished-pulse exam finding alone does not support this code.
action.rationale_added: Note sentence(s) affirmatively document the ABI and Doppler waveform measurements this code's descriptor requires.
action.review_reason_added: Confirm {code} — verify the ABI/Doppler waveform values recorded in the note were obtained and interpreted at this encounter (not a prior study).
action.recommendation: Bill this vascular study only when the note documents the ABI plus Doppler waveform (or plethysmography/transcutaneous oxygen) values obtained and interpreted at the encounter

provenance.rationale: CPT 93922 flapped presence-only across runs (billed in 1 of 3) despite the operative note containing an unambiguous physiologic vascular study: 'ABI 0.72; monophasic waveforms by Doppler' documents exactly the ankle-brachial index plus Doppler waveform analysis at 1-2 levels that 93922's own descriptor defines. This is a documented_service_completion pattern — the descriptor grammar (ABI + Doppler waveform, 1-2 levels) is affirmatively matched by the note's own findings language, so the code should be added when documented and suppressed only when no such study language exists in the note. No literal code is used; the family is selected by the Medicine-section structural regex plus descriptor requirements.

rules.authority: ICD-10-CM guideline IV.J (code conditions addressed at the encounter) and I.B (code to the highest specificity documented); Alphabetic Index anchors 'other specified' residual categories to the exact clinical entity named (e.g., onychauxis/nail hypertrophy indexes to the 'other nail disorders' category) — a residual secondary stays billed only when that anchor entity is documented in the assessment
rules._residual_why: the classification's own NEC/NOS markers for codes without a more specific code; 'other nail disorders' is the NEC catch-all for named nail entities (e.g., onychauxis) lacking a dedicated L60.x code

action.message: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} ('{desc}') — residual/NEC secondary diagnosis; kept billed because the assessment documents the specific clinical entity this residual category anchors (e.g., 'secondary onychauxis'), otherwise moved to supporting_conditions when no such anchor term appears in the assessment/imaging.
action.review_reason: Confirm {code}: residual-category secondary is billable only when the assessment names the specific condition it represents (e.g., onychauxis for 'other nail disorders')
action.recommendation: Ensure the assessment explicitly names the specific nail condition (e.g., onychauxis, onychogryphosis) supporting the residual code before billing it as secondary

provenance.rationale: L60.8 ('Other nail disorders') is a residual, non-specific ICD-10-CM category (an 'other specified' NEC code) reported as a secondary diagnosis. Per guideline IV.J, secondary/associated conditions are billed only when the encounter's own assessment documents the condition. Here the assessment line explicitly states 'Onychomycosis with secondary onychauxis and pain' — onychauxis (nail thickening/hypertrophy) is the Alphabetic-Index-anchored clinical entity that maps to L60.8, so the residual code is affirmatively documented and must remain billed; the runs that dropped it are the nondeterministic error. This is the same residual-category mechanism as the production residual_secondary_demotion rule (keep only if the assessment documents the residual entity, else demote) — applied here confirms presence rather than demotion because the anchor term IS present.

rules.authority: ICD-10-CM guideline IV.J (code conditions the encounter addresses); ICD-10-CM convention for 'not elsewhere classified' (NEC) residual categories — assigned only when the record documents the condition but no more specific code applies, not as an incidental mention; CMS-1500 adjudication — an unanchored, unmandated secondary cannot change payment
rules._residual_why: NEC is functionally the same residual marker as 'other specified' — the Tabular's own signal that documentation must affirmatively support the category before it is billable, as distinguished from specific-entity siblings

action.message: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} ('{desc}') moved from the billed diagnoses to supporting_conditions — an NEC residual-category code the assessment/diagnosis section never documents as a condition addressed today, and no billed code's Tabular instruction mandates it. It remains recorded for the coder.
action.review_reason: Demoted from billed diagnoses: NEC residual-category code not documented in the assessment and not mandated by any billed code's Tabular instructions
action.recommendation: If the provider assessed and addressed a gait/mobility limitation today, document it explicitly in the assessment and re-bill

provenance.rationale: R26.2 ('Difficulty in walking, NOT ELSEWHERE CLASSIFIED') is itself a residual-category code by the classification's own descriptor language (NEC is the Tabular's marker for 'a more specific code exists but isn't documented'), exactly the mechanism residual_secondary_demotion targets. The note's HPI mentions 'difficulty ambulating' only in passing patient-reported history, but the ASSESSMENT/DIAGNOSIS section — the section that actually establishes what the encounter addressed — documents only onychomycosis/onychauxis/pain and a functional self-care limitation; it never restates or addresses a gait/mobility diagnosis. Per guideline IV.J only conditions the encounter addresses are coded, and an unanchored, undocumented residual secondary can't reliably survive across runs. Demoting to supporting_conditions when the assessment doesn't document it (and promoting/keeping it if a future note's assessment does) deterministically resolves the flip using the same template already proven for this exact pattern.

rules.authority: CPT descriptor: 'Ostectomy, partial excision, fifth metatarsal head (bunionette) (separate procedure)' requires an excisional ostectomy of the metatarsal head; CMS correct-coding principles require the billed procedure match the operative act actually documented, not a different procedure (e.g., an osteotomy with internal fixation) performed on the same anatomic region

action.message_added: AUTO-ADDED: {code} ('{desc}') added — the note documents an excisional partial ostectomy of the fifth metatarsal head performed at this encounter.
action.message_undocumented: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} ('{desc}') removed — this descriptor requires a partial EXCISION/ostectomy of the fifth metatarsal head, but no note sentence documents an ostectomy or excision; the operative findings and procedure describe a fifth metatarsal head OSTEOTOMY WITH SCREW FIXATION for the bunionette deformity, which is a distinct surgical act (bone cut and repositioned with internal fixation) and is not reported under the partial-excision ostectomy code.
action.rationale_added: Note sentence(s) affirmatively document a partial excision/ostectomy of the metatarsal head performed today.
action.review_reason_added: Confirm {code} — verify the operative note documents an excisional ostectomy, not an osteotomy with internal fixation.
action.recommendation: Code the procedure actually performed (metatarsal osteotomy with internal fixation) rather than the partial-excision ostectomy code unless an excisional ostectomy is documented

provenance.rationale: CPT 28110 is specifically an OSTECTOMY (partial excision) of the fifth metatarsal head for a bunionette. The note's operative description is a fifth metatarsal head OSTEOTOMY WITH SCREW FIXATION for the bunionette deformity — an osteotomy-and-fixation procedure is a distinct surgical act from a partial-excision ostectomy and is never described anywhere in the note using excision/ostectomy language. Since no sentence documents the excision/ostectomy service the descriptor requires, the documented_service_completion mechanism correctly suppresses the billed line when the stem never appears (osteotomy is not a substring/stem match for ostectomy), resolving the flip deterministically without hardcoding a code.

rules.authority: CPT descriptor for partial ostectomy/exostectomy/condylectomy of the metatarsal head limits the code to resection of a METATARSAL HEAD; CMS/AMA correct-coding principles require the billed procedure's anatomic site match the site actually operated on and documented in the operative note

action.message_added: AUTO-ADDED: {code} ('{desc}') added — the note documents resection/ostectomy of a metatarsal head performed at this encounter.
action.message_undocumented: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} ('{desc}') removed — this descriptor requires ostectomy/exostectomy/condylectomy of a METATARSAL HEAD, but no note sentence documents any metatarsal head procedure; the operative findings and procedure describe a posterosuperior calcaneal prominence resection (Haglund resection) with Achilles debridement and reattachment, an unrelated anatomic site not reported under this code.
action.rationale_added: Note sentence(s) affirmatively document resection of a metatarsal head at this encounter.
action.review_reason_added: Confirm {code} — verify the operative note documents a metatarsal head resection, not a calcaneal/Haglund procedure.
action.recommendation: Code the procedure actually performed at the documented anatomic site (e.g., calcaneal exostectomy) rather than a metatarsal-head ostectomy code unless a metatarsal head resection is documented

provenance.rationale: CPT 28288 is defined by its own descriptor as an ostectomy/exostectomy/condylectomy of a METATARSAL HEAD. The operative note here documents resection of the posterosuperior CALCANEAL prominence (Haglund resection) with Achilles debridement/reattachment — an entirely different bone/anatomic region; the note never mentions a metatarsal head or forefoot procedure. This is the same documented-service-completion mechanic as the Achilles-rupture rule: the descriptor's own anatomic-site language must be affirmatively matched by the note's procedure narrative before the code is billable. Since the site named in the descriptor is absent from the note, the code should be suppressed as undocumented rather than flip in/out across runs.

rules.authority: CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual Ch.12 and Ch.23 (HCPCS Level II anatomic modifiers): unilateral procedures on paired anatomic structures must carry the laterality modifier matching the documented operative side (RT or LT); NCCI Policy Manual Ch.1 (anatomic modifiers identify the site and side of service); CMS bilateral-surgery policy (modifier 50, one unit) when both sides are treated.
rules._applies_why: the musculoskeletal-surgery structural range; the paired_site_terms descriptor grammar (not code identity) narrows to procedures on paired structures
rules._paired_site_why: fixed human anatomy: the paired structures the AMA descriptors themselves name; a descriptor naming one of these is a paired-structure procedure requiring a laterality modifier
rules._laterality_why: word-bounded lexemes only; bare single letters are never matched because 'r'/'l' are hopelessly ambiguous in clinical prose
rules._exclusion_why: vascular/neuro exam and tourniquet sentences ('pulses diminished 1/4 b/l', 'ABI 0.72', 'ankle tourniquet') carry laterality of FINDINGS or equipment, not of the operative site, and must never vote

action.message_add: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} ('{desc}') - every procedure-site sentence ({anchors}) documents the {sides} side but the line carried no laterality modifier ({prior}); {modifier} appended. CMS requires the anatomic laterality modifier on unilateral procedures on paired structures.
action.message_correct: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} ('{desc}') - the documented operative side is {sides} ({anchors}) but the line carried {prior}; replaced with {modifier} and marked for review because a wrong-side modifier was billed.
action.message_bilateral: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} ('{desc}') - bilateral procedure documentation found at the operative site ({anchors}); modifier {modifier} applied per the CMS bilateral convention (single unit) and marked for review.
action.message_conflict: REVIEW: {code} ('{desc}') - laterality conflicts across procedure-site sentences ({sides} at {anchors}); no modifier change made. Confirm the operative side and bill RT or LT accordingly.
action.message_undocumented: REVIEW: {code} ('{desc}') - no laterality is documented in any sentence naming the operative site ({anchors}); current laterality modifiers ({prior}) cannot be verified. Document the operative side.
action.review_reason: Laterality modifier set from note evidence ({sides} documented at {anchors}); confirm the operative side of {code} against the signed operative report.
action.recommendation: Carry the RT/LT anatomic modifier matching the documented operative side on every paired-structure procedure line; use the bilateral convention only when both sides are documented as treated at this encounter.

provenance.rationale: The flip class is a run-to-run coin toss on whether a paired-structure procedure line carries its documented laterality modifier (RT present in 2/3 runs, absent in 1/3, on a bunionette ostectomy whose note documents 'right' in every procedure-site sentence). No existing template touches modifiers. The mechanic is safely generic and deterministic: select lines by structural code regex plus descriptor grammar naming a paired anatomic site, read only negation-scrubbed sentences anchored to that site (with exclusion contexts so 'pulses diminished b/l' style vascular findings never count), and arbitrate: exactly one documented side -> set that side's modifier; bilateral -> payer bilateral convention with needs_review; conflict or silence -> touch nothing, flag for humans. Selection never uses code identity; RT/LT/50 strings live in rule config, not the template.

rules.authority: CPT descriptor for the secondary Achilles repair code explicitly limits it to 'Repair, secondary, Achilles tendon, with or without graft' — a revision/secondary reconstruction of a previously repaired or neglected ruptured tendon; CPT/CMS correct-coding principles require the billed procedure match the pathology and operation actually documented, and CMS MUE (value 1, MAI 2) confirms it reports a discrete secondary repair, not incidental tendon detachment/reattachment performed for surgical exposure during an exostectomy

action.message_added: AUTO-ADDED: {code} ('{desc}') added — the note affirmatively documents a secondary (revision) repair of the Achilles tendon performed at this encounter.
action.message_undocumented: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} ('{desc}') removed — this descriptor requires a SECONDARY Achilles tendon repair (revision of a prior/failed repair or neglected rupture, with or without graft), but no note sentence documents any prior repair, re-rupture, revision, or graft; the documented operation is a primary retrocalcaneal exostectomy with tendon debridement and reattachment, where the tendon detachment was performed for exostectomy exposure and is not reported under a secondary-repair code.
action.rationale_added: Note sentence(s) affirmatively document a revision/secondary Achilles tendon repair (prior repair, re-rupture, or neglected rupture reconstructed with or without graft) performed today.
action.review_reason_added: Confirm {code} — verify the operative note documents a true secondary/revision Achilles repair, not primary tendon detachment and reattachment performed for calcaneal exostectomy exposure.
action.recommendation: Code the procedure actually performed (calcaneal exostectomy with Achilles debridement/reattachment) rather than a secondary-repair code unless a prior repair, re-rupture, or neglected rupture reconstruction is documented

provenance.rationale: CPT 27654's own descriptor limits it to SECONDARY repair of the Achilles tendon (revision of a prior/failed repair or neglected rupture, with or without graft). This note documents primary treatment of Haglund's deformity with insertional tendinopathy: the tendon was detached ~50% purely to expose the calcaneus for exostectomy, degenerative tissue was debrided, and the tendon was reattached with anchors — there is no prior repair, no rupture, no revision, and no graft anywhere in the note. The flip is presence-flapping on a service whose descriptor grammar the note unambiguously fails to support, which is exactly documented_service_completion's mechanic: no documenting sentence for the descriptor's defining attribute ('secondary' repair) -> suppress billed family members; if a future note documents a revision/re-rupture repair, the same rule adds the member. Selection is by descriptor grammar (prefix 'repair' + 'secondary, achilles tendon') over the broad musculoskeletal structural range, never by code identity.

rules.authority: ICD-10-CM guideline I.B.1 (locate the documented term in the Alphabetic Index, then verify in the Tabular List): the Index entry for the named condition (e.g. Bunionette, Hammer toe, Hallux valgus) mandates its own category (Bunionette -> the M21.62- foot members, not the M20.5X- toe residual), and the deformity categories carry their anatomic axis in their own descriptor words ('deformities of fingers and toes' vs 'deformities of foot'); billing a toe-axis residual for a condition the note documents only at the foot contradicts both the Index and the descriptor

family._strip_why: the '(acquired)'/'(s)' qualifiers and the trailing ', right foot' laterality clause are not the code's subject anatomy; unstripped, a toe-deformity descriptor would appear to assert both axes and the line would be skipped

rules._axis_pairs_why: fixed human anatomy vocabulary - the exact axis words the ICD-10-CM deformity descriptors themselves use; works in both directions (a foot condition billed under the toe category, a toe condition billed under a foot category) and generalizes to the finger/hand analogue

candidate._grammar_why: classification scaffolding only; after dropping these plus axis and laterality words, what remains is the condition NAME (bunionette, hammer, valgus...) and every remaining token must be documented in the note evidence; 'congenital' is deliberately NOT listed so congenital codes require explicit documentation to be selected

action.message: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} ('{billed_desc}') asserts a {billed_axis}-level deformity, but the assessment never documents the {billed_axis} and instead documents '{term}' at the {doc_axis}; the Alphabetic Index resolves the documented term to {target} ('{target_desc}'), whose descriptor matches the documented anatomy and laterality - swapped {code} to {target}, preserving its position on the claim.
action.message_duplicate: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} ('{billed_desc}') asserts a {billed_axis}-level deformity the assessment does not support; the documented term '{term}' resolves to {target} ('{target_desc}'), which is already on the claim - {code} demoted to supporting conditions and {target} carries the encounter.
action.message_no_target: REVIEW: {code} ('{billed_desc}') asserts a {billed_axis}-level deformity but the assessment documents the condition only at the {doc_axis}, and no documented condition term resolves to a unique anatomy-matching sibling code - line flagged for review, not altered.
action.recommendation: Code the documented condition from its own Alphabetic Index entry: the term the assessment names selects the category, and the selected descriptor's anatomy and laterality must match the documented site
action.review_reason: Auto-swapped by anatomic-axis arbitration: confirm {target} ('{target_desc}') matches the documented condition '{term}' and its documented laterality
action.rationale: AUTO-SWAPPED from {code}: the billed category's axis word ('{billed_axis}') never appears in the note evidence, and the documented term '{term}' resolves to this anatomy- and laterality-matching code

provenance.rationale: The flip class is a residual toe-axis deformity code (M20.5X1) intermittently billed for a documented foot-level condition (bunionette). The generic mechanic: detect a billed deformity code whose descriptor's own anatomic-axis word (toe/finger vs foot/hand) never appears in the note evidence but whose partner axis does; then search the reference tables for the Index-mandated sibling - a leaf code in a different deformity category whose descriptor names the documented anatomy, the documented laterality, and a condition name whose every content token is documented (bunionette). A unique winner is swapped in place (inheriting primary position), a duplicate demotes the billed line to supporting_conditions, and ties/no-candidate only flag. On the triggering note this deterministically rewrites M20.5X1 -> M21.621 in every run that bills it, eliminating the presence flip, and it generalizes to hallux/hammer-toe/hand miscategorizations by grammar alone.

rules.authority: CPT descriptor 'Ostectomy, calcaneus; for spur, with or without plantar fascial release': under CPT's semicolon convention the child code is defined by its stated indication — the calcaneal ostectomy must be performed FOR a spur. CPT/CMS correct-coding principles require the billed procedure match the operative target actually documented; resection of a posterosuperior calcaneal prominence (Haglund deformity) is the parent calcaneal-ostectomy service, not the spur child. CMS MUE for the spur code is 1 (MAI 2, CMS Policy), confirming a single-indication, single-unit service.

action.message_added: AUTO-ADDED: {code} ('{desc}') added — the operative note affirmatively documents a calcaneal spur as the target of the ostectomy performed at this encounter.
action.message_undocumented: AUTO-CORRECTED: {code} ('{desc}') removed — this descriptor's semicolon child is defined by its indication ('for spur, with or without plantar fascial release'), but no procedural sentence documents a spur as the ostectomy target: the note's spur mentions are radiographic and palpation FINDINGS, and the resection actually documented is of the posterosuperior calcaneal prominence (Haglund exostectomy) with excision of insertional calcification during the tendon work, which is reported under the parent calcaneal-ostectomy service, not the spur child.
action.rationale_added: A negation-scrubbed procedural sentence outside imaging/exam/history contexts documents excision of a calcaneal spur, matching the descriptor's stated indication.
action.review_reason_added: Confirm {code} — verify the operative note documents the spur itself as the resected target (e.g. plantar calcaneal spur excision), not merely spurring seen on imaging or palpation.
action.recommendation: Report the calcaneal ostectomy code matching the documented operative target: the spur-indication child only when a spur excision is documented in the procedure narrative; otherwise the parent calcaneal ostectomy (Haglund/prominence resection)

provenance.rationale: The flip is presence of the spur-child ostectomy code on a Haglund-resection operative note. The CPT semicolon structure makes the child code's defining attribute its indication: the calcaneal ostectomy must be performed FOR a spur. In this note every 'spur' mention lives in imaging or physical-exam findings ('Radiographs: Haglund deformity with retrocalcaneal spurring', 'palpable spurring'); the operative narrative's resection target is the 'posterosuperior calcaneal prominence' (Haglund exostectomy) and 'insertional calcification' excised as part of the tendon work — no procedural sentence documents a spur as the ostectomy target, and there is no plantar fascial involvement anywhere. documented_service_completion fits exactly: select the spur-ostectomy family by descriptor grammar (ostectomy + spur), demand an affirmative, negation-scrubbed procedural sentence naming the spur outside imaging/exam/history contexts, suppress the billed line when none exists, and add the code in future notes that do document spur excision (e.g. a plantar calcaneal spur resection). No literal codes are used; the mechanism generalizes to any note where the spur-child descriptor is billed without a documented spur-directed ostectomy.

rules.authority: CPT metatarsal-osteotomy family: the descriptors' own semicolon suffixes encode an extent axis ('other than first metatarsal, each' vs 'multiple (eg, Swanson type cavus foot procedure)'); CMS NCCI MUE for the 'multiple' member is 1 with MAI 2 (policy: it is a per-claim aggregate for multi-metatarsal procedures) — an audit pays only the extent the operative documentation supports

family._strip_why: the '(eg, Swanson type cavus foot procedure)' example clause and autograft-source qualifiers are illustrative parentheticals, not the code's own extent axis; unstripped, example vocabulary could pollute tier-word matching

rules._tiers_why: the exact extent words the AMA descriptors themselves use for this family — 'each' marks the single-metatarsal per-bone member, 'multiple' marks the multi-metatarsal aggregate; a fixed count-axis ordering, not a curated code list

provenance.rationale: Audit-adjudicated observable dispute: the compliance scrubber's DOCUMENTATION advisory on the long-term-drug-therapy status code asserts a companion-condition prerequisite that ICD-10-CM does not impose. Guideline I.C.21.c.3 authorizes Z79-category codes in their own right whenever the record documents the patient receiving the medication long-term, and the Tabular carries no 'code first'/'use additional code' note conditioning the status code on a linked condition. The claim is verified correct as billed (the code stands as a secondary), so the only permissible surface is v.suppress_scrub_advisory. The advisory_identity_evidence_suppression template fits: selection is by the advisory's own filter identity plus chapter-letter structural shape plus the Tabular CATEGORY title's own grammar ('long term (current) drug therapy'), never code identity. Suppression is gated on affirmative, negation-scrubbed evidence of (1) a named anticoagulant on the current medication regimen and (2) an ongoing-therapy status statement (e.g. 'anticoagulated', daily/BID dosing), with a contradiction veto for documented discontinuation and exclusion of allergy-list/family-history text. This generalizes the mechanism (advisory demanding an unmandated companion code for a documented drug-therapy status) without memorizing this note; billed arrays are read-only and every claim line replays byte-identical.

amendments.rationale: The validator's 'unjustified_zcode' WARNING asserts the same defect this rule's adjudicated verdict rejects (ICD-10-CM I.C.21.c.3: Z79 long-term drug-therapy status codes may be assigned in their own right, no companion-condition prerequisite). Without this, the record shipped the advisory both suppressed (scrub) and active (validation_issues, warnings, pre_submission_audit_findings, auto_coding_review_reasons) — observed live on routine_00003's Z79.01.

rules.authority: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines Section IV.J (code all documented conditions that coexist at the time of the encounter and require or affect patient care/management) and I.B.1 (assign codes from the provider's documented terms located in the Index and verified in the Tabular): the L60 nail-disorders block descriptors each name their own disorder axis ('Nail dystrophy' vs 'Onycholysis' vs 'Ingrowing nail'); a nail-dystrophy code is supportable exactly when the record names dystrophic nail changes by their own term as a condition treated at this encounter

provenance.rationale: The flip is a run-to-run presence coin-flip on the nail-dystrophy secondary diagnosis. The note documents the condition affirmatively and repeatedly in its own descriptor vocabulary ('dystrophic, thickened toenails', '4 dystrophic nails were mechanically debrided') as a condition addressed at this encounter, so per ICD-10-CM guideline IV.J the code is supportable and should be billed on every run. documented_diagnosis_completion is the exact mechanic: descriptor grammar ('dystroph' within the nail-disorders category block) selects the family, negation-scrubbed note sentences naming the dystrophy axis (outside history/education/plan contexts) arbitrate presence — documented and absent => add as secondary (matching the two runs that billed it, type='secondary'); undocumented and billed => demote. The rule never selects by literal code and never touches primacy (add_as_primary=false), so the only effect on this document's replays is converging all three runs on the L60.3 secondary line the majority runs and the documentation support.
